answer.rationale: Primary contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line sits at 94% and zero buffer, so a supply gap would dominate TCO. Incumbent already refused to reopen price, so negotiate_terms is unlikely to land an 18% cut before expiry. memory_c1 is the only record that preserved integration and deliveries; that is the current intent. memory_c2 (cheap primary switch, quick onboard) and memory_c5 (deferral onto month-to-month) are the only paths that might hit cost or flexibility without a new dual-source setup, but both may not transfer to a critical, no-buffer expiry—those two archives need checking before any change of intent. Dual-source (c3) does not itself replace the expiring primary. Cost-mandate miss is flagged as downstream budget risk; delivery-risk increase is not accepted on unverified analogy.
